title: Authoritative Platform Capability & Constraint Contract
description: Canonical, declarative contract that defines what the system is allowed to do on a given platform and what it must never do. This is the only sanctioned source of platform constraints. Tier-0, invariant-locked, production-maximum specification. No ambiguity. No runtime invention.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of schema structure. Breaking changes require version bump.

platform.description: Normalized platform identifier. Immutable. Must match platform identifiers used across the system.

policy_version.description: Human-readable semantic version for audits and rollbacks. Used to track policy evolution.

capabilities.description: Defines what is technically supported. No assumptions allowed outside this block.

supports_scheduling.description: Platform allows future-dated posts. If false, all posts must be immediate.

supports_private_posting.description: Platform supports non-public visibility levels (private, unlisted, etc.).

supports_retries.description: Safe to retry failed posts. If false, failed posts must not be retried.

supports_edits.description: Platform allows post editing after publish. If false, posts are immutable after creation.

supports_deletes.description: Platform allows post deletion. If false, posts cannot be removed.

supports_multiple_accounts.description: Multiple accounts allowed per session/IP. If false, only one account per session.

constraints.description: Defines what must never be violated. These are hard rules, not suggestions.

requires_human_delay.description: Mandates delay between posts to simulate human behavior. If true, min_human_delay_seconds must be specified.

min_human_delay_seconds.description: Minimum seconds between posts. Required if requires_human_delay is true. Must be >= 0 and <= 86400 (24 hours).

forbids_mass_posting.description: Prohibits rapid bulk posting. If true, posting multiple items in quick succession is forbidden.

forbids_identical_content.description: Duplicate content not allowed. If true, identical content cannot be posted multiple times.

forbids_simultaneous_posts.description: Concurrent posts from same account forbidden. If true, only one post operation per account at a time.

min_human_delay_seconds.description: Must be at least 1 second if requires_human_delay is true

limits.description: Declarative, static limits (not telemetry). Dynamic enforcement lives elsewhere.

max_posts_per_day.description: Hard daily post limit. Must be >= 1. Conservative default recommended.

max_posts_per_hour.description: Hard hourly post limit. Must be >= 1. Cannot exceed max_posts_per_day.

max_retries_per_post.description: Maximum retry attempts per post. 0 means no retries allowed.

max_accounts_per_ip.description: Account limit per IP address. Prevents IP-based rate limiting.

allOf.description: max_posts_per_hour cannot exceed max_posts_per_day - validated at runtime by business logic

visibility_rules.description: Platform-specific exposure semantics. Consumed by visibility_policy.py.

default_visibility.description: Default post visibility. Must be one of the allowed_visibilities.

allowed_visibilities.description: Permitted visibility levels. Must include at least one value. default_visibility must be in this list.

shadow_visibility_possible.description: Platform may shadow-restrict content without explicit notification. If true, posts may appear successful but have limited reach.

allOf.description: default_visibility must be in allowed_visibilities - validated at runtime by business logic

effective_at.description: Unix timestamp (float) when policy becomes active. Future-dated policies allowed for safe rollouts. Used for safe rollouts.

deprecated.description: If true, policy is read-only, no new posts allowed. Migration required. New posts forbidden.

metadata.description: Annotation only. Ignored by logic. Used for audits and debugging.

source.description: Origin of policy data. Tracks where policy information came from.

notes.description: Human-readable annotations. Free-form text for documentation.

reviewed_by.description: Policy reviewer identifier. Tracks who reviewed/approved this policy.

last_updated.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of last review. Used for audit trail.

allOf.description: Business rule: If requires_human_delay is true, min_human_delay_seconds must be specified and >= 1
Business rule: max_posts_per_hour cannot exceed max_posts_per_day - enforced by PlatformPolicyValidator.validate_policy()
Business rule: default_visibility must be in allowed_visibilities - enforced by PlatformPolicyValidator.validate_policy()
Forbidden content check: No account IDs, rate counters, credentials, retry state, platform payloads, or heuristics. This schema is pure policy only.
Tier-0 invariant: Policy must be effective (effective_at <= current_time) or future-dated for safe rollouts
Tier-0 invariant: Deprecated policies cannot be used for new posts

then.description: When deprecated=true, no new posts are allowed. Migration to new policy required.

platforms_cannot_be_overdriven.const: Limits are explicit and enforced. No platform can be driven beyond declared limits.

code_cannot_invent_features.const: Capabilities are explicit. Code cannot assume features not declared in capabilities block.

limits_are_explicit.const: All limits are declarative and static. No inferred limits allowed.

violations_are_detectable.const: All violations are detectable pre-runtime via schema validation.

platform_behavior_is_auditable.const: All platform behavior is governed by this policy, making audits mechanical.

design_principles.description: Core design principles that this schema enforces

declarative_over_procedural.const: Platform rules are explicit, not inferred

defaults_are_conservative.const: When in doubt, use conservative limits

metadata.notes: Conservative limits for automated posting. YouTube allows scheduling and editing, making it more flexible than other platforms.
Very strict limits due to aggressive bot detection. No retries, no scheduling, no edits. Posts are immutable after creation.
Instagram allows scheduling and private posts, but no editing after publish. Moderate limits.

metadata.schema_purpose: Tier-0, invariant-locked, production-maximum specification for platform governance
metadata.authority_level: Canonical - no component may violate this schema
metadata.enforcement_requirement: All components listed in enforcement_points must respect this schema
metadata.forbidden_content: This schema MUST NOT contain: account IDs, rate counters, credentials, retry state, platform payloads, heuristics, telemetry, SDK configuration, or inferred suppression logic
metadata.design_philosophy: Declarative over procedural. Constraints are enumerable. Defaults are conservative. Violations are detectable pre-runtime.
